An office tower on Miller Street in Manchester is completely covered in solar panels. They are used to create some of the energy used by the insurance company inside. When the tower was first __26__ in 1962, it was covered with thin square stones. These small square stones became a problem for the building and continued to fall off the face for 40 years until a major renovation was __27__ . During this renovation the building's owners, CIS, __28__ the solar panel company, Solar century. They agreed to cover the entire building in solar panels. In 2004, the completed CIS tower became Europe's largest __29__ of vertical solar panels. A vertical solar project on such a large __30__ has never been repeated since.
paragraphs.translationZh: 曼彻斯特米勒街的一座办公楼完全被太阳能电池板覆盖。它们用于产生保险公司内部使用的一些能源。 1962年始建塔时，塔身覆盖着薄薄的方石。这些方形的小石头成为了建筑的一个问题，并且在 40 年间不断从表面脱落，直到进行了一次重大整修。在这次翻修过程中，大楼业主 CIS 咨询了太阳能电池板公司 Solar century。他们同意用太阳能电池板覆盖整个建筑。 2004 年，竣工的 CIS 塔成为欧洲最大的垂直太阳能电池板集合体。此后，如此大规模的垂直太阳能项目再也没有重复过。

paragraphs.sourceText: Covering a skyscraper with solar panels had never been done before, and the CIS tower was chosen as one of the "10 best green energy projects". For a long time after this renovation project, it was the tallest building in the United Kingdom, but it was __31__ overtaken by the Mill bank Tower.
paragraphs.translationZh: 用太阳能电池板覆盖摩天大楼是前所未有的，CIS塔被选为“十大最佳绿色能源项目”之一。这次改造工程后的很长一段时间里，它都是英国最高的建筑，但最终被米尔银行大厦超越。

paragraphs.sourceText: Green buildings like this aren't __32__ cost-efficient for the investor, but it does produce much less pollution than that caused by energy __33__ through fossil fuels. As solar panels get __34__ , the world is likely to see more skyscrapers covered in solar panels, collecting energy much like trees do. Imagine a world where building the tallest skyscraper wasn't a race of __35__ , but rather one to collect the most solar energy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 像这样的绿色建筑对于投资者来说不一定具有成本效益，但它产生的污染确实比通过化石燃料生产能源造成的污染要少得多。随着太阳能电池板变得越来越便宜，世界上可能会看到更多的摩天大楼覆盖太阳能电池板，就像树木一样收集能量。想象一下这样一个世界：建造最高的摩天大楼不是一场高度竞赛，而是一场收集最多太阳能的竞赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

paragraphs.sourceText: Some College Students Are Angry That They Have to Pay to Do Their Homework
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些大学生对他们必须付费做作业感到愤怒

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Digital learning systems now charge students for access codes needed to complete coursework, take quizzes, and turn in homework. As universities go digital, students are complaining of a new hit to their finances that's replacing—and sometimes joining—expensive textbooks: pricey online access codes that are required to complete coursework and submit assignments.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 数字学习系统现在向学生收取完成课程作业、参加测验和上交作业所需的访问代码费用。随着大学走向数字化，学生们抱怨他们的财务状况受到了新的打击，他们正在取代（有时甚至加入）昂贵的教科书：完成课程和提交作业所需的昂贵的在线访问代码。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The codes—which typically range in price from $ 80 to $ 155 per course—give students online access to systems developed by education companies like McGraw Hill and Pearson. These companies, which long reaped big profits as textbook publishers, have boasted that their new online offerings, when pushed to students through universities they partner with, represent the future of the industry.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这些代码（每门课程的价格通常从 80 美元到 155 美元不等）让学生可以在线访问由 McGraw Hill 和 Pearson 等教育公司开发的系统。这些公司长期以来作为教科书出版商获得了巨额利润，他们吹嘘说，当他们通过合作大学向学生推出新的在线产品时，代表了该行业的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) But critics say the digital access codes represent the same profit-seeking ethos (观念) of the textbook business, and are even harder for students to opt out of. While they could once buy second-hand textbooks, or share copies with friends, the digital systems are essentially impossible to avoid.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但批评者表示，数字访问代码代表了与教科书行业相同的逐利理念，学生更难选择退出。虽然他们曾经可以购买二手教科书，或与朋友分享副本，但数字系统基本上是无法避免的。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) "When we talk about the access code we see it as the new face of the textbook monopoly (垄断), a new way to lock students around this system," said Ethan Senack, the higher education advocate for the U.S. Public Interest Research Group, to BuzzFeed News. "Rather than $250 (for a print textbook) you're paying $ 120," said Senack. "But because it's all digital it eliminates the used book market and eliminates any sharing and because homework and tests are through an access code, it eliminates any ability to opt out."
paragraphs.translationZh: D）“当我们谈论访问代码时，我们将其视为教科书垄断的新面孔，一种将学生锁定在该系统周围的新方式，”美国公共利益研究小组的高等教育倡导者伊森·塞纳克（Ethan Senack）对 BuzzFeed 新闻说道。 “你需要支付 120 美元，而不是 250 美元（印刷版教科书），”Senack 说。 “但因为它都是数字化的，所以它消除了二手书市场并消除了任何共享，而且因为作业和测试是通过访问代码进行的，所以它消除了任何选择退出的能力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Sarina Harpet, a 19-year-old student at Virginia Tech, was faced with a tough dilemma when she first started college in 2015—pay rent or pay to turn in her chemistry homework. She told BuzzFeed News that her freshman chemistry class required her to use Connect, a system provided by McGraw Hill where students can submit homework, take exams and track their grades. But the code to access the program cost $ 120—a big sum for Harper, who had already put down $ 450 for textbooks, and had rent day approaching.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 萨琳娜·哈佩特 (Sarina Harpet)，一名 19 岁的弗吉尼亚理工大学学生，2015 年刚开始上大学时，她面临着一个艰难的困境——支付房租还是交化学作业。她告诉 BuzzFeed News，她的新生化学课要求她使用 Connect，这是 McGraw Hill 提供的一个系统，学生可以在其中提交作业、参加考试并跟踪成绩。但访问该程序的代码要花费 120 美元，这对哈珀来说是一笔巨款，他已经为教科书支付了 450 美元，而且租借日即将到来。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) She decided to wait for her next work-study paycheck, which was typically $ 150- $ 200, to pay for the code. She knew that her chemistry grade may take a dive as a result. "It's a balancing act," she said. "Can I really afford these access codes now?" She didn't hand in her first two assignments for chemistry, which started her out in the class with a failing grade.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 她决定等待下一次勤工俭学的工资（通常为 150 至 200 美元）来支付代码费用。她知道她的化学成绩可能会因此而下降。 “这是一种平衡行为，”她说。 “我现在真的能负担得起这些访问代码吗？”她没有交出前两份化学作业，这导致她在课堂上成绩不及格。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The access codes may be another financial headache for students, but for textbook businesses, they're the future. McGraw Hill, which controls 21% of the higher education market, reported in March that its digital content sales exceeded print sales for the first time in 2015. The company said that 45% of its $ 140 million revenue in 2015 "was derived from digital products."
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 访问代码对于学生来说可能是另一个财务难题，但对于教科书企业来说，它们就是未来。控制着21%高等教育市场的麦格劳希尔公司3月份报告称，其数字内容销售额在2015年首次超过印刷版销售额。该公司表示，其2015年1.4亿美元收入中的45%“来自数字产品”。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) A Pearson spokesperson told BuzzFeed News that "digital materials are less expensive and a
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 培生集团发言人告诉 BuzzFeed News，“数字材料更便宜，而且

paragraphs.sourceText: good investment" that offer new features, like audio texts, personalized knowledge checks and expert videos. Its digital course materials save students up to 60% compared to traditional printed textbooks, the company added. McGraw Hill didn't respond to a request for comment, but its CEO David Levin told the Financial Times in August that "in higher education, the era of the printed textbook is now over."
paragraphs.translationZh: 良好的投资”，提供新功能，如音频文本、个性化知识检查和专家视频。该公司补充说，与传统印刷教科书相比，其数字课程材料可以为学生节省高达 60% 的费用。麦格劳希尔大学没有回应置评请求，但其首席执行官戴维·莱文 (David Levin) 在八月向英国《金融时报》表示，“在高等教育领域，印刷教科书的时代现已结束。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The textbook industry insists the online systems represent a better deal for students. "These digital products aren't just mechanisms for students to submit homework, they offer all kinds of features," David Anderson, the executive director of higher education with the Association of American Publishers, told BuzzFeed News. "It helps students understand in a way that you can't do with print homework assignments."
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 教科书行业坚持认为在线系统对学生来说更划算。美国出版商协会高等教育执行董事戴维·安德森 (David Anderson) 告诉 BuzzFeed News：“这些数字产品不仅仅是学生提交作业的机制，它们还提供各种功能。” “它可以帮助学生以一种打印作业无法做到的方式理解。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) David Hunt, an associate professor in sociology at Augusta University, which has rolled out digital textbooks across its math and psychology departments, told BuzzFeed News that he understands the utility of using systems that require access codes. But he doesn't require his students to buy access to a learning program that controls the class assignments. "I try to make things as inexpensive as possible," said Hunt, who uses free digital textbooks for his classes but designs his own curriculum. "The online systems may make my life a lot easier but I feel like I'm giving up control. The discussions are the things where my expertise can benefit the students most."
paragraphs.translationZh: J) David Hunt 是奥古斯塔大学社会学副教授，该大学已在其数学和心理学系推出了数字教科书，他告诉 BuzzFeed News，他了解使用需要访问代码的系统的实用性。但他并不要求学生购买控制课堂作业的学习计划。 “我试图让东西尽可能便宜，”亨特说，他在课堂上使用免费的数字教科书，但设计了自己的课程。 “在线系统可能让我的生活变得更轻松，但我觉得我正在放弃控制。讨论是我的专业知识最能让学生受益的事情。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) A 20-year-old junior at Georgia Southern University told BuzzFeed News that she normally spends $ 500-$ 600 on access codes for class. In one case, the professor didn't require students to buy a textbook, just an access code to turn in homework. This year she said she spent $ 900 on access codes to books and programs. "That's two months of rent," she said. "You can't sell any of it back. With a traditional textbook you can sell it for $ 30 - $ 50 and that helps to pay for your new semester's books. With an access code, you're out of that money. "
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 佐治亚南方大学一名 20 岁的大三学生告诉 BuzzFeed News，她通常会花费 500 至 600 美元购买课程访问码。在一个案例中，教授并不要求学生购买教科书，只要求学生提供交作业的访问代码。她说今年她花了 900 美元购买书籍和程序的访问代码。 “这是两个月的房租，”她说。 “你不能把它卖回来。传统的教科书你可以以 30 - 50 美元的价格出售，这有助于支付你新学期的书本费用。有了访问代码，你就没有那么多钱了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Benjamin Wolverton, a 19-year-old student at the University of South Carolina, told BuzzFeed News that "it's ridiculous that after paying tens of thousands in tuition we have to pay for all these access codes to do our homework." Many of the access codes he's purchased have been required simply to complete homework or quizzes. "Often it's only 10% of your grade in class." he said. "You're paying so much money for something that hardly affects your grade—but if you didn't have it, it would affect your grades enough. It would be bad to start out at a B or C." Wolverton said he spent $ 500 on access codes for digital books and programs this semester.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 南卡罗来纳大学 19 岁学生本杰明·沃尔弗顿 (Benjamin Wolverton) 告诉 BuzzFeed News，“在支付了数万美元的学费后，我们还必须支付所有这些访问代码才能完成作业，这太荒谬了。”他购买的许多访问代码只是为了完成作业或测验。 “通常这只是你课堂成绩的 10%。”他说。 “你花这么多钱买的东西几乎不会影响你的成绩——但如果你没有它，它就会对你的成绩产生足够的影响。从 B 或 C 开始就不好了。”沃尔弗顿说，他本学期花费了 500 美元购买数字图书和程序的访问代码。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Harper, a poultry (家禽) science major, is taking chemistry again this year and had to buy a new access code to hand in her homework. She rented her economics and statistics textbooks for about $ 20 each. But her access codes for homework, which can't be rented or bought second-hand, were her most expensive purchases: $ 120 and $ 85.
paragraphs.translationZh: 家禽科学专业的 M) Harper 今年再次选修化学，必须购买新的访问代码才能交作业。她以每本 20 美元左右的价格租了经济学和统计学教科书。但她的家庭作业访问代码不能租用或购买二手，但却是她最昂贵的购买物品：120 美元和 85 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) She still remembers the sting of her first experience skipping an assignment due to the high prices. "We don't really have a missed assignment policy," she said. "If you miss it, you just miss it. I just got zeros on a couple of first assignments. I managed to pull everything back up. But as a scared freshman looking at their grades, it's not fun."
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 她仍然记得第一次因为高价而跳过任务的经历的刺痛。 “我们确实没有错过作业的政策，”她说。 “如果你错过了，那你就错过了。我的第一次作业只得了零分。我设法把所有的事情都拉回来。但作为一个害怕的新生，看着他们的成绩，这并不有趣。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. A student's yearly expenses on access codes may amount to their rent for two months.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 学生每年用于访问代码的费用可能相当于两个月的租金。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The online access codes may be seen as a way to tie the students to the digital system.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 在线访问代码可被视为将学生与数字系统联系起来的一种方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. If a student takes a course again, they may have to buy a new access code to submit their assignments.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 如果学生再次参加课程，他们可能需要购买新的访问代码才能提交作业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. McGraw Hill accounts for over one-fifth of the market share of college textbooks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 麦格劳·希尔 (McGraw Hill) 占据大学教科书市场份额五分之一以上。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Many traditional textbook publishers are now offering online digital products, which they believe will be the future of the publishing business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 许多传统教科书出版商现在提供在线数字产品，他们相信这将是出版业的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. One student complained that they now had to pay for access codes in addition to the high tuition.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一名学生抱怨说，现在除了高额学费外，他们还必须支付访问密码的费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Digital materials can cost students less than half the price of traditional printed books according to a publisher.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 据出版商称，数字材料的学生费用还不到传统印刷书籍价格的一半。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. One student decided not to buy her access code until she received the pay for her part-time job.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一名学生决定在收到兼职工资之前不购买访问代码。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Online systems may deprive teachers of opportunities to make the best use of their expertise for their students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 在线系统可能会剥夺教师为学生充分利用其专业知识的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Digital access codes are criticized because they are profit-driven just like the textbook business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 数字访问代码受到批评，因为它们就像教科书业务一样以利润为导向。

paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Losing your ability to think and remember is pretty scary. We know the risk of dementia (痴呆症) increases with age. But if you have memory slips, you probably needn't worry. There are pretty clear differences between signs of dementia and age-related memory loss.
paragraphs.translationZh: 失去思考和记忆的能力是非常可怕的。我们知道患痴呆症的风险随着年龄的增长而增加。但如果你有记忆失误，你可能不必担心。痴呆症和与年龄相关的记忆丧失的迹象之间存在明显差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: After age 50, it's quite common to have trouble remembering the names of people, places and things quickly, says Dr. Kirk Daffner of Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston.
paragraphs.translationZh: 波士顿布莱根妇女医院的柯克·达夫纳 (Kirk Daffner) 医生表示，50 岁以后，很难快速记住人名、地名和事物的名字是很常见的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The brain ages just like the rest of the body. Certain parts shrink, especially areas in the brain that are important to learning, memory and planning. Changes in brain cells can affect communication between different regions of the brain. And blood flow can be reduced as blood vessels narrow.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大脑和身体其他部位一样都会老化。某些部分会萎缩，尤其是大脑中对学习、记忆和计划很重要的区域。脑细胞的变化会影响大脑不同区域之间的交流。随着血管变窄，血流量也会减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Forgetting the name of an actor in a favorite movie, for example, is nothing to worry about. But if you forget the plot of the movie or don't remember even seeing it, that's far more concerning, Daffner says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，忘记最喜欢的电影中演员的名字就不用担心。但达夫纳说，如果你忘记了电影的情节，或者甚至不记得看过它，那就更令人担忧了。

paragraphs.sourceText: When you forget entire experiences, he says, that's "a red flag that something more serious may be involved." Forgetting how to operate a familiar object like a microwave oven, or forgetting how to drive to the house of a friend you've visited many times before can also be signs of something going wrong.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说，当你忘记整个经历时，这就是“一个危险信号，可能涉及更严重的事情”。忘记如何操作微波炉等熟悉的物体，或者忘记如何开车去你以前去过多次的朋友家也可能是出现问题的迹象。

paragraphs.sourceText: But even then, Daffner says, people shouldn't panic. There are many things that can cause confusion and memory loss, including health problems like temporary stoppage of breathing during sleep, high blood pressure, or depression, as well as medications ( 药物) like antidepressants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但达夫纳说，即使如此，人们也不应该惊慌。有很多因素会导致意识混乱和记忆丧失，包括睡眠期间呼吸暂时停止、高血压或抑郁等健康问题，以及抗抑郁药等药物。

paragraphs.sourceText: You don't have to figure this out on your own. Daffner suggests going to your doctor to check on medications, health problems and other issues that could be affecting memory. And the best defense against memory loss is to try to prevent it by building up your brain's cognitive (认知的) reserve, Daffner says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您不必自己解决这个问题。达夫纳建议去看医生，检查药物、健康问题和其他可能影响记忆的问题。达夫纳说，防止记忆丧失的最佳方法是通过建立大脑的认知储备来预防记忆丧失。

paragraphs.sourceText: "Read books, go to movies, take on new hobbies or activities that force one to think in novel ways," he says. In other words, keep your brain busy and working. And also get physically active, because exercise is a known brain booster.
paragraphs.translationZh: “读书、看电影、培养新的爱好或活动，迫使人们以新颖的方式思考，”他说。换句话说，让你的大脑保持忙碌和工作。并且还要积极锻炼身体，因为运动是众所周知的大脑助推器。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: A letter written by Charles Darwin in 1875 has been returned to the Smithsonian Institution Archives (档案馆) by the FBI after being stolen twice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 查尔斯·达尔文于 1875 年写的一封信，在两次被盗后，被联邦调查局归还给史密森学会档案馆。

paragraphs.sourceText: "We realized in the mid-1970s that it was missing," says Effie Kapsalis, head of the Smithsonian Insitution Archives. "It was noted as missing and likely taken by an intern (实习生), from what the FBI is telling us. Word got out that it was missing when someone asked to see the letter for research purposes," and the intern put the letter back. "The intern likely took the letter again once nobody was watching it."
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们在 20 世纪 70 年代中期意识到它丢失了，”史密森学会档案馆馆长艾菲·卡普萨利斯 (Effie Kapsalis) 说道。 “据联邦调查局告诉我们的信息，这封信被注意到丢失了，很可能是实习生拿走的。当有人出于研究目的要求查看这封信时，有消息称这封信丢失了，”实习生把信放了回去。 “当没有人看到这封信时，实习生可能会再次拿走这封信。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Decades passed. Finally, the FBI received a tip that the stolen document was located very close to Washington, D.C. Their art crime team recovered the letter but were unable to press charges because the time of limitations had ended. The FBI worked closely with the Archives to determine that the letter was both authentic and definitely Smithsonian's property.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几十年过去了。最后，联邦调查局收到线报，称被盗文件位于华盛顿特区附近。他们的艺术犯罪小组找到了这封信，但由于时效已过，无法提出指控。联邦调查局与档案馆密切合作，确定这封信是真实的，并且绝对是史密森尼的财产。

paragraphs.sourceText: The letter was written by Darwin to thank an American geologist, Dr. Ferdinand Vandeveer Hayden, for sending him copies of his research into the geology of the region that would become Yellowstone National Park.
paragraphs.translationZh: 达尔文写这封信是为了感谢美国地质学家费迪南德·范德维尔·海登博士向他寄来了他对后来成为黄石国家公园的地区的地质研究的副本。

paragraphs.sourceText: The letter is in fairly good condition, in spite of being out of the care of trained museum staff for so long. "It was luckily in good shape," says Kapsalis, "and we just have to do some minor things in order to be able to unfold it. It has some glue on it that has colored it slightly, but nothing that will prevent us from using it. After it is repaired, we will take digital photos of it and that will be available online. One of our goals is to get items of high research value or interest to the public online."
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管这封信长期没有经过训练有素的博物馆工作人员看管，但它的状况相当良好。 “幸运的是，它状况良好，”卡普萨利斯说，“我们只需要做一些小事情就可以展开它。它上面有一些胶水，使它稍微变色，但没有什么会阻止我们使用它。修复后，我们将为它拍摄数码照片，并将其发布到网上。我们的目标之一是在网上提供具有高研究价值或公众感兴趣的物品。”

paragraphs.sourceText: It would now be difficult for an intern, visitor or a thief to steal a document like this. "Archiving practices have changed greatly since the 1970s," says Kapsalis, "and we keep our high value documents in a safe that I don't even have access to."
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，实习生、访客或小偷都很难窃取这样的文件。 “自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，归档实践发生了巨大变化，”Kapsalis 说道，“我们将高价值文件保存在我什至无法接触的保险箱中。”
